questions.stem: APRV (airway pressure release ventilation) is mainly used for which condition?
questions.explanation: The burn-anesthesia chapter lists APRV among proposed modes for severe ARDS. This does not establish routine superiority for surgery or a universal first-choice mode.
questions.citation: Elisha, Heiner, & Nagelhout (2023), Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed., Chapter 39, printed p. 925

questions.stem: What are goals of a recruitment maneuver? Select 2.
questions.explanation: Recruitment aims to reopen collapsed alveoli and improve oxygenation. Better aeration of perfused lung can reduce shunt, although excessive pressure can impair circulation.
questions.citation: Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 6, printed pp. 159–160

questions.stem: A typical manual recruitment maneuver uses what pressure and duration?
questions.explanation: The lecture describes about 30–40 cmH2O held for more than 10 seconds ("30 for 30"). Nurse Anesthesia's obese-patient table uses 35–40 cmH2O for 8–10 seconds and calls for monitoring for hypotension and bradycardia.
questions.citation: Elmore, Anesthesia Ventilators: slide 64; Elisha, Heiner, & Nagelhout (2023), Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed., Chapter 48, printed p. 1105

questions.stem: Recruitment maneuvers should be avoided in which patient?
options: Healthy patient with atelectasis after induction
Laparoscopic case with falling SpO2 (peripheral oxygen saturation)
questions.explanation: Avoid in neurotrauma and pneumothorax; also watch for hypotension.
questions.citation: Elmore, Anesthesia Ventilators: slide 64

questions.stem: Right after a successful manual recruitment, the patient is switched back to the ventilator with zero PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure). What is the main concern?
questions.explanation: Without suitable end-expiratory support, reopened lung units can collapse again. Maintaining recruitment must be balanced against overdistension and hemodynamic effects.
questions.citation: Elisha, Heiner, & Nagelhout (2023), Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed., Chapter 48, printed p. 1105; Ehrenwerth, Eisenkraft, & Berry (2021), Anesthesia Equipment: Principles and Applications, 3rd ed., Chapter 6, printed p. 159

questions.stem: Per the instructor, how is a manual recruitment maneuver done?
options: Open the APL (adjustable pressure-limiting valve) fully and release the bag quickly
Close the APL (adjustable pressure-limiting valve) halfway; squeeze the bag ≥10 s to a PIP (peak inspiratory pressure) near 40
Raise RR to 30 breaths/min for one full minute
Press the O2 flush for 10 seconds straight
questions.explanation: Note: close APL ½ way, squeeze reservoir bag ≥10 sec, PIP about 40.
questions.citation: Elmore, Anesthesia Ventilators: slide 64

questions.stem: Per the pediatric parameters table, what PEEP (positive end-expiratory pressure) is suggested?
questions.explanation: With pressure support set to zero, the selected PEEP supplies the continuous baseline airway pressure. In this example, that pressure is 5 cmH2O; CPAP (continuous positive airway pressure) alone does not guarantee alveolar ventilation.
questions.citation: Elisha, Heiner, & Nagelhout (2023), Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed., Chapter 16, printed p. 279

questions.stem: Per the pediatric table, what peak inspiratory pressure limit applies in pressure control?
questions.explanation: The lecture's pediatric table lists PIP under 28 cmH2O in pressure control. Don't confuse it with Nurse Anesthesia Table 16.7, where 28 cmH2O is an adult plateau-pressure target.
questions.citation: Elmore, Anesthesia Ventilators: slide 65; Elisha, Heiner, & Nagelhout (2023), Nurse Anesthesia, 7th ed., Chapter 16, printed p. 277

questions.stem: Per the pediatric table, inspiratory time ranges from:
questions.explanation: Inspiratory time 0.4 (infants) to 1.0 (adolescents).
questions.citation: Elmore, Anesthesia Ventilators: slide 65

questions.stem: Pediatric tidal volume per the lecture table is:
questions.explanation: 5–8 mL/kg IBW (ideal body weight) with pressure support of 4–6 cmH2O.
questions.citation: Elmore, Anesthesia Ventilators: slide 65
